description: The pie chart represents the distribution of various entity types in a dataset, comparing their relative proportions. The chart is divided into 18 slices, each representing a distinct category. The largest slice, labeled "Composite Mention" and colored blue, occupies approximately 32% of the chart. The second-largest slice, "Protein" in orange, accounts for around 15%. Other notable slices include "DNA" in green (6%), "Chemical Family" in red (5%), "Disease" in purple (5%), "Cell Type" in dark red (5%), and "Drug" in brown (4%). The remaining slices are smaller, with labels such as "Frequency", "Cell Line", "Dosage", "Strength", "Form", "Gene Or Gene Product", "Disease Or Phenotypic Feature", "Specific Disease", "Reason", "Route", "Chemical Entity", "Sequence Variant", "Modifier", "RNA", "Disease Class", "Organism Taxon", and "Mutation", and occupy proportions ranging from 3% to less than 1%. The chart includes percentage labels inside each slice, and the slices are arranged in descending order of their proportions. No legend is present, and none of the slices are visually emphasized.
